title: A worker that is retried after running out of turns is told what its earlier attempt did and said, not only handed its files
tier_reason: changes the retry brief in the drain; git reverts it
ask: Today a turn-limit retry (resume_brief in hq/drain.py) gets the held patch applied into its worktree and one paragraph saying the earlier attempt ran out. It is not shown what that attempt did or concluded, so it re-derives its own plan. Every session is now written to hq/data/runs/workers/<run>/<item>-drain-work.jsonl as it runs. When building the retry brief, read the previous attempt's stream (the newest file for the item), compact it the way server._compact_event does, and include: the last ~40 plain lines (what it read, edited, ran, said), and the last thing it said in full. Cap the block at ~4,000 characters. Say plainly in the brief that this is the previous attempt's own record. Prove it on one item by hand and show the brief.
first_action: Read resume_brief and task_prompt in hq/drain.py and _compact_event in hq/server.py; write a helper that finds the newest session file for an item and returns the compacted tail.
source_message: Daniel, 2026-09-21, asked whether a retried task continues where the previous one left off; the answer was 'files yes, memory no', and this closes the gap.

result:
Done. Here's what changed and what it now does.

**The change.** `hq/drain.py` grew `prior_session(item)`, which finds the previous attempt's recorded session for that item and returns the part worth carrying forward: the last forty things it read, changed, ran and said, one line each, then the last thing it said in full. `task_prompt` inserts that block right after the item and the reasons an earlier attempt was sent back, so a retried worker gets the record before it plans. The whole block is capped at 4,000 characters, and a long closing reply is trimmed so it can never eat the room the action lines need.

Three judgement calls inside it, each one something the real recorded sessions forced:

- **The newest session is not always the one to read.** One item in the queue has eleven sessions on top of each other that were refused at the account's usage ceiling — two lines apiece — sitting above the thirteen-minute attempt that actually did the work. The helper takes the most recent session that did at least a few things.
- **Paths are rewritten.** Every file a worker touches is recorded under its own worktree, which by retry time is deleted. Those prefixes are stripped, so the brief reads `Read world/farm.gd`, not a 90-character dead path.
- **Tool output is dropped, failures are kept.** Forty lines of file contents is not a record of what an attempt was doing; the line naming the call is.

**The proof.** `python3 hq/drain.py --brief <item-id>` prints the brief the next attempt would be given, takes no lock and runs nothing. On the real recorded sessions, for the item Sam has been retrying, the block comes out at 2,523 characters and opens:

> WHAT YOUR EARLIER ATTEMPT DID — this is that attempt's own record, written down as it worked, not a summary anybody wrote for you. It stopped before it finished: it was cut off at the account's usage ceiling. Read it before you plan, and continue its work instead of starting the item again from the beginning.
>
> The last things it read, changed, ran and said:
>
> ```
>   Read hq/data/decisions/Q-108.json
>   Ran: find tools -iname "*door_backdrop*" -o -iname "*profile_door*"
>   Read tools/profile_door_backdrop.gd
>   Searched for '_backdrop_view|backdrop|CanvasLayer|SubViewport' in world/farm.gd
>   Read world/farm.gd
>   said: Good, all three (`SimWorld`, `SpeciesDefs`, `WorldLayout`) are global classes…
>   Edited tools/capture_through_walls.gd (−3 +6 lines)
>   Wrote tools/capture_through_walls.tscn (7 lines)
> ```
>
> The last thing it said:
> …

That is a worker that had already found the backdrop code, written a capture tool and a scene, and would otherwise have started from `ls`.

**Tests.** New: `hq/tests/test_drain_resume.py`, twelve checks against sessions written for the test — the ceiling stubs are skipped, the current run is never read back to itself, the cap holds under a 12,000-character closing reply, the dead paths are gone, and the item still comes first in the brief. It is wired into the same CI job as the existing HQ test, and both are green. `docs/HOW_WORK_ORIGINATES.md` records the behaviour in the same change. Nothing here touches the game, so the Godot suites are not in play.

**One thing you should know.** Those eleven refusals were not one bad night: for four hours the timer kept picking the same two items up and getting turned away at the usage ceiling, writing an empty session each time. The hold that is supposed to prevent exactly that is not catching it. Filed below.

follow_ups.title: Stop the work queue from starting items while the account's usage window is dry
follow_ups.first_action: In hq/data/runs/workers/, eleven consecutive sessions for w72dee30012f and wdab4785be1c between 23:20 and 02:05 recorded error LIMITED with two-line streams. Read unattended_hold() in hq/drain.py against those timestamps, work out why it let those runs start, and make a refusal at the ceiling hold the queue back until the window resets.
follow_ups.why: The queue spent four hours starting work it could not run, and each refusal leaves an empty record that the new retry brief then has to step over.

follow_ups.title: Correct the process doc where it says how often the work queue runs on its own
follow_ups.first_action: docs/HOW_WORK_ORIGINATES.md says the timer runs every two hours; commit 6b9400b changed it to every twenty minutes. Fix the line and check the rest of that section against hq/systemd/.
follow_ups.why: The doc is the studio's account of how its own queue runs, and it now describes a schedule the machine no longer keeps.

landed.note: Tomas's attempt was ported onto today's file by hand after two rebases failed. `python3 hq/drain.py --brief <id>` prints what the next attempt would be told, and its test runs in the build.
